claim: Let \(X\) be a compact metric space and let \(J\) be a closed lattice ideal of \(C(X)\). Then \(J\) is semiprojective if and only if either \(J=0\), or there is a nonempty clopen absolute neighbourhood retract \(U\subseteq X\) such that \(J=\{f\in C(X):f|_{X\setminus U}=0\}\). Equivalently, for closed \(F\subseteq X\), the ideal \(I_F=\{f\in C(X):f|_F=0\}\) is semiprojective exactly when \(X\setminus F=\varnothing\) or \(X\setminus F\) is a clopen absolute neighbourhood retract. If \(X\setminus F\) is not closed, then \(c_0\) is a contractive lattice retract of \(I_F\). In particular, for the middle-third Cantor set \(K\subset[0,1]\), \(I_K\) is not semiprojective.
integrity: The proof explicitly constructs the retract and separates theorem-level deductions from literature-search evidence. Search non-detection is not treated as a proof of novelty, and no numerical experiment is used as proof.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns closed lattice ideals of \(C(X)\) for compact metric \(X\); it does not classify ideals in arbitrary Banach lattices or nonmetrizable \(C(X)\)-spaces.
It does not answer the general extension-permanence question for semiprojectivity; the Cantor pullback is excluded because its kernel \(I_K\) is already non-semiprojective.
The disjoint-bump retract construction is elementary and may be known in other contexts; literature non-detection is not a proof of novelty.
No independent audit has been performed.
title: Semiprojective ideals of \(C(X)\): the clopen-ANR classification
